title: What fraction of the big triangle is X M N?
description: In a triangle, M and N are the midpoints of two sides. A line from a corner to the midpoint of the opposite side halves a triangle, and doing this twice shows that the small triangle is a quarter of the big one.
teaching_notes: One idea: a line from a corner to the midpoint of the opposite side halves the triangle, because the two halves have equal bases and the same height. Watch for students who say the small triangle is half of the big one.

video_script.why: The child applies the equal bases, same height method of the solved example twice, to halve the triangle and then halve it again.
video_script.substitution: Join N to Y, halve the triangle XYZ, then halve the triangle XNY.
video_script.anchor: the book's triangle XYZ with M on XY and N on XZ, the midpoints of their sides, and the dotted line NY
video_script.payoff_line: Triangle X M N is one quarter of triangle X Y Z

final_answer.spoken: triangle X M N is one quarter of triangle X Y Z

video_script.fraction_reading: a half and a quarter are said as words
never_show: the answer before the answer beat
maths_rules: N is the midpoint of XZ, so XN = NZ; triangles XNY and NYZ have equal bases on XZ and the same height from Y, so they have equal areas
the two equal triangles fill ΔXYZ, so ΔXNY = 1/2 of ΔXYZ
M is the midpoint of XY, so XM = MY; triangles XMN and MYN have equal bases on XY and the same height from N, so they have equal areas
the two equal triangles fill ΔXNY, so ΔXMN = 1/2 of ΔXNY
check: if ΔXYZ = 8, then ΔXNY = 4 and ΔXMN = 2, and 2 is 1/4 of 8
video_script.design: One triangle all video. A line to a midpoint halves a triangle, and it is done twice. The check uses a made-up area of eight.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find what fraction of triangle X Y Z is triangle X M N.

beats.on_screen: Join NY. XN = NZ and the height from Y is the same, so area (XNY) = 1/2 × area (XYZ)

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step one, join N to Y. It cuts the triangle into X N Y and N Y Z.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>The bases X N and N Z are equal, and both triangles have the same height from Y.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Their areas are equal, so triangle X N Y is half of triangle X Y Z.

beats.on_screen: In triangle XNY: XM = MY and the height from N is the same, so area (XMN) = 1/2 × area (XNY)

marks.tri: triangle X N Y is outlined and N M is drawn

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step two, look at triangle X N Y. The line N M goes to the middle of X Y.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>The bases X M and M Y are equal, and both parts share the height from N.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Triangle X M N is half of triangle X N Y.

marks.chain: the two halves are chained: 1/2 of 1/2 of area (XYZ)

narration: <bookmark mark='chain'/>Step three, triangle X M N is half of a half of triangle X Y Z.
<bookmark mark='quarter'/>Half of a half is a quarter.

beats.on_screen: check: area (XYZ) = 8, area (XNY) = 4, area (XMN) = 2, and 2 is 1/4 of 8

marks.two: area (XMN) = 2 is written, and 2 is 1/4 of 8

narration: <bookmark mark='eight'/>Step four, check with an area of eight.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Half of eight is four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Half of four is two, and two is a quarter of eight.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Triangle X M N is one quarter of triangle X Y Z.
